convoLines.text: "I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one."
Terrence has an edge today — something curdled.

"It's my older sister, Kate. Was taken. She raised me more than our mother did. Boring. That is what they wrote down. Some nights I dream about the pods -- rows of them, humming. I wake up and I can't tell if it was a dream or a broadcast.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Anyway, that's me."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
"Ha." Not amused. "I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to keep everyone fed. There are people from my old life I'd rather never find me. That's all. There. You happy?"
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Yeah. Sorry. It's -- never mind. Forget I said anything." They look away, embarrassed at having wanted something.
"Still on what was on their mind."
"I've got fires to light — metaphorical ones. Mostly."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Got a read on anyone here yet? Who should I be watching? Hm."
"Same. But keep your eyes open — some people here are performing, not surviving."
"This one — Rubber Seeds. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Watch the quiet ones. Not the loud — the loud tell you everything. The quiet are either thinking or planning, and you can't tell which until it matters. Don't look away from this."
"Still on your read on people here."
"Yes. Absolutely. I've been hoping you'd ask." (A little too quickly.)
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? I mean it."
"Good question." "Have you heard what they're calling Lockpick? Alejandra is pushing 'Loud-Eyes'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"I have opinions about the name. I am saving them for when they count."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"We're done for now. Not done-done. For now."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About what happened to my taken kin — You talk to it -- the System. Have you ever asked? About the taken -- about Kate?"
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Still nothing on Kate. I told you about the pods -- I keep thinking about them. The humming. Some nights I'm sure it's a dream. Other nights I'm sure it's not."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"That again?" Terrence sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Yeah. Sorry. It's -- never mind. Forget I said anything." They look away, embarrassed at having wanted something.
"Sure — Still on what was on their mind. That's still where we are."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
"You said you're still figuring everyone out. Figure anything out yet? Anyone you're watching?"
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
Alejandra shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Here's what I think — Still on that personal stuff."
They relax, a fraction. This is going well.
You show them Hickory Nuts — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Yeah? What's up?"

"You want to know about that? Okay." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Have you heard what they're calling Nightlight? Alejandra is pushing 'Big Ugly'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"Go. But sit with what I said."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"About what happened to my taken kin — Have you heard anything? About the taken. The pods. Anything at all."
They nod. "Okay."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
Terrence looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Yeah. Sorry. It's -- never mind. Forget I said anything." They look away, embarrassed at having wanted something.
"Like I said — Still on what was on their mind."
"Right. Action time. You know where to find me."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Hear me out — We never finished talking about that personal stuff — we wandered off it, 7 days back. 'You show them Hickory Nuts — where it grows, how to tell it apart.
They nod slowly, committing it to memory.…' We still owe what's been happening a proper ending, too."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
At the ridge the ground is torn up. Something was here, recently, and it wasn't careful. Alejandra's hand finds your sleeve. You leave together, faster than you came.
"This one — Baobab. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Still on that personal stuff. That's still where we are. I need you to hear that."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took you — The Alibi Chain, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
You show them White Oak Acorns — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one."
"Still nothing on Kate. I told you about the pods -- I keep thinking about them. The humming. Some nights I'm sure it's a dream. Other nights I'm sure it's not."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? Not that it matters."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
"You're wrong." Too fast. Terrence looks away. "Just... drop it, okay?"
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Yeah. Sorry. It's -- never mind. Forget I said anything." They look away, embarrassed at having wanted something.
"As I said — Still on what was on their mind."
"Right. Go on, then."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what was on their mind."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? At night I count the stars and name them after people."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
You walk to the hollow with Wei. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on their secret."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Don't tell anyone I told you. What's on your mind?"
"Since Abigail died... I keep expecting to see Abigail at the fire. Stupid."
"I keep turning over the last thing Abigail said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
You show them Chickweed — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.

d9: SYSTEM: "INTRUDER REPELLED. The pantry’s aroma is now classified as a defensive liability. The audience is chanting the defenders’ names. Fan clubs are forming. This is how it starts."
d9: ◈ AUDIENCE TRIAL — SYSTEM: "The audience wants an encore. A trial, then — smaller this time, but televised." Haul 1,000 kcal to the pantry within 3 days. Reward: integration, and a lesson.

d9: ◈ ARC III — ENGINES. SYSTEM: "VIEWERSHIP MILESTONE. Organic unit demonstrates compounding capability. Resonance protocols unlocked." — Your gifts deepen. Used in sequence, they resonate. The village is no longer just surviving. It is becoming something.
d10: ◈ SYSTEM: "Ooh. NEIGHBORS. You know what neighbors are for? STORYLINES. Go knock — worst case, it's CONTENT. Best case? The show gets BIGGER."
d10: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 50. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 4."
d10: SYSTEM: Oh! It has a NAME. You all love names.
